title: 2005 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 3
statement: Prove that every \((a, b)\)-tileable rectangle contains a rectangle of these dimensions.

solutions.text: An \(m \times n\) rectangle, \(m \leq n\), does not contain a \(\max \{1,2 a\} \times 2 b\) rectangle if and only if \(m<2 a\) or \(n<2 b\). But if either of these is the case, then the square closest to the center of the rectangle cannot be paired with any other square of the rectangle to form a domino of type \((a, b)\), so the rectangle cannot be \((a, b)\)-tileable.
